text:
The Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics invites applications for a full-time Assistant Professor of Teaching with potential for security of employment (equivalent to tenure track). Professor of Teaching faculty are Academic Senate faculty members whose expertise and responsibilities center on undergraduate education, and scholarly analysis/improvement of teaching methods. 

The appointee will be expected to carry out high-level and innovative teaching consistent with the broad goals of the department. The appointee may be required to teach up to six quarter-long undergraduate courses per year (e.g., two courses per quarter: 2-2-2) in departmental undergraduate curricula as assigned by the department chair. Teaching assignments are based on enrollment, scope (classroom, field, laboratory) and needs of the unit as well as career stage of the appointee. The appointee’s primary teaching responsibilities are likely to include ARE 113 Marketing Management, ARE 135 Agribusiness Marketing Plan Development, ARE 136 Managerial Marketing, and ARE 133 Introduction to Behavioral Economics. The appointee may be asked to develop additional coursework in Marketing and Consumer Behavior. Other courses that the appointee may be asked to teach include ARE 100A and 100B Microeconomics, ARE 106 Econometrics, ARE 130 Agricultural Markets, ARE 155 Operations Research & Management Science, ARE 157 Analysis for Operations & Production Management, and ARE 194 Senior Research Thesis. Other responsibilities include undergraduate student advising.

The appointee will also be expected to demonstrate continued professional growth and contribute to the university mission through service activities. Examples of professional growth may involve some or all of the following professional contributions and attainments: (i) research and publication in the candidate’s subject-matter discipline, (ii) pedagogical or curricular innovation, (iii) research and publication on pedagogy, (iv) professional activity in professional organizations, and (v) academic leadership within the University beyond normal service obligations. 

This recruitment is being conducted at the assistant rank. The resulting hire will be at the assistant rank, regardless of the proposed appointee's qualifications.

Qualified applicants must have a Ph.D. or equivalent in economics, agricultural economics, applied economics, marketing, or a closely related discipline at the time of appointment, and demonstrated expertise in areas including but not limited to consumer behavior, quantitative marketing, demand analysis, behavioral economics, market structure, pricing, product differentiation, or industrial organization. Other preferred qualifications include documented success in some or all of the following areas as related to applied economics and marketing: teaching large undergraduate classes, use of evidence based teaching practices, use of modern instructional technology including virtual models, ability to identify and develop effective teaching strategies for diverse student populations, conducting disciplinary and pedagogical research. 

All application materials must be received by January 5, 2027 to be assured full consideration. Applicants should submit materials online at: https://recruit.ucdavis.edu. Please include your 
1. Curriculum Vitae
2. Statement of Teaching Accomplishments and Interests (not to exceed two pages, 12 point double spaced 1-inch margins, and normal character spacing, e.g. Times New Roman). Please discuss prior teaching experience, teaching approach, and future teaching interests. This can include, for example, specific efforts and accomplishments, and future plans to support student success.
3. Statement of Research Accomplishments (not to exceed two pages, 12 point double spaced 1-inch margins, and normal character spacing)
4. At least one and up to three working papers or publications.
5. Three recommendation letters.
6. An Authorization to Release Information (https://aadocs.ucdavis.edu/your-resources/forms-and-checklists/forms/authorization-release-form.pdf)

For more information on this position and UC Davis in general, please visit the following web site: https://www.ucdavis.edu/ or contact the search committee chair at jhilscher@ucdavis.edu. 

Initial review of applications will be conducted using anonymized versions of the Statement of Teaching Accomplishments and Interests. Applications demonstrating sufficient potential based on this review will be advanced to full review. 

This is an academic year (9-month), Assistant Professor of Teaching with potential for security of employment (equivalent to tenure track) position.

Salary: 

The salary range for this position is $145,900 - $173,700 (annual). “Off-scale salaries” and other components of pay, i.e., a salary that is higher than the published system-wide salary at the designated rank and step, are offered when necessary to meet competitive conditions, qualifications, and experience.


As a condition of employment, the finalist will be required to disclose if they are subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct, are currently being investigated for misconduct, left a position during an investigation for alleged misconduct, or have filed an appeal with a previous employer.

“Misconduct” means any violation of the policies or laws governing conduct at the applicant’s previous place of employment, including, but not limited to, violations of policies or laws prohibiting sexual harassment, sexual assault, or other forms of harassment, or discrimination, as defined by the employer.

• APM - 035: Affirmative Action and Nondiscrimination in Employment (https://www.ucop.edu/academic-personnel-programs/_files/apm/apm-035.pdf)

To implement this process, UC Davis requires all applicants for any open search to complete, sign, and upload the form entitled, "Authorization to Release Information" (AOR) (https://academicaffairs.ucdavis.edu/sites/g/files/dgvnsk2376/files/media/documents/authorization-release-form.pdf) into UC RECRUIT as part of their application. If an applicant does not include the signed authorization with the application materials, the application will be considered incomplete, and as with any incomplete application, will not receive further consideration.
